title: Whiting on toast with aubergine and runner beans

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a plain store-cupboard staple such as capers, olive oil and crusty bread, with no jars, stock pots or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Aubergines, runner beans, tomatoes, basil and whiting fillets are all everyday-priced items at a mainstream supermarket in July.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only two frying pans, a knife, a board and a toaster or grill, and pan-frying fish fillets is within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: Two aubergines with four tomatoes, 200g runner beans and four fillets on four slices of toast is a sensible lunch for four, and the frying times would cook everything through without burning.

honest_times.reason: Cubing aubergines, slicing beans and garlic and chopping tomatoes, plus tending the frying pans, fits within the 40 minutes printed in total for a standard pace.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon, basil and chilli flakes, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm aubergine, tomato and runner bean pile on toast suits a July lunch, and the aubergine makes up the bulk of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, brief British English that a neighbour could follow without any restaurant jargon.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a proper meal of fish, plenty of vegetables and bread that a family would happily eat again.
